habit_scope: Superintendent order on 2-story light-wood: wall/ceiling finishes already hanging (P14); then interior doors/trim; coatings; floor coverings after wall/ceiling finishes. CMHC Ch2+22+23+24. Cabinets named in Ch23. No invented finish schedule.
how_it_is_done: CMHC Ch2 Interior Finishes: ceiling, wall and floor finishes, shelving and cabinets. Finishing carpentry for interior doors, frames and trim plus stair balusters/handrails usually immediately after floor/wall/ceiling finishes have been prepared for painting and varnishing. About two weeks. Then Paint, Cabinets and Fixtures (paint first). Cabinets named in both stage titles — quote both, do not invent which week. B&D (US): trim then paint then floor. Keep both orders; one sequence on the job. AF&PA (US): store interior doors, trim, flooring, cabinetwork in the building; wet plaster must dry first. Stair structure is P08 — do not rewrite.

Ch22: Floor coverings must not be laid until interior wall and ceiling finishes are completed. Wood strip: not until basement concrete has cured and gypsum finishing is done so humidity has moderated; keep flooring warm and dry. Installed wet, it shrinks and opens joints (named). Underlay (when required): annular grooved nails ≤150 mm (6 in) along edges and 200 mm (8 in) OC both ways in the field; nails ≥19 mm (3/4 in) for 6 mm (1/4 in) underlay, ≥22 mm (7/8 in) for 7.9 mm (5/16 in). Staples or screws may also be used. Fig 166: 6 mm (1/4 in) expansion at the plate (or manufacturer); field fasteners 45° at the tongue. AF&PA (US): 25/32 T&G may go on subfloor; underlayment for resilient/carpet; ≥1/2 in expansion at parallel partitions and exterior walls, hidden by base/toe. Keep both expansion numbers. Strip-flooring nail lengths live in Table 42 (p 309) — table not extracted this pass; CLASS annular/spiral nails, do not invent pennies. FM 5-426 8d every joist is Army TO technique, not this habit.

Ch23: Interior doors usually pre-hung. Shim (wood shingles) between jamb and RO studs at ends of jambs and at hinge and latch locations. Plumb and square; screw or nail jambs through the wedges; nails in pairs; cut wedges flush. Stops 10×32 mm (3/8 × 1-1/4 in) finishing-nailed after the door is hung. Casings 5–6 mm (3/16–1/4 in) off the inner jamb edge; finish nails to studs and jambs about 400 mm (16 in) apart; countersink and fill. Knob 860–960 mm (34–38 in) from the floor. Fig 170 clearances: 2 mm head/hinge, 1 mm latch, 19 mm bottom.

Ch24: coatings = paint, varnish, stain, lacquer. Sealers/primers seal wood grain or drywall/plaster before topcoats. Water-solvent products named. Apply ≥10°C (50°F). No invented wall-paint coat-count beyond primer-then-topcoat as composition, not a schedule. Varnish: two thin coats with light sanding between named for most residential work — varnish, not a latex wall count.

Ch2 Paint, Cabinets and Fixtures: painting at the beginning of that stage, then ceramic tile backsplashes, then electrical devices and equipment (that leftover is P16). Ch23 millwork/cabinets often with interior trim, usually before strip is sanded or resilient is laid. Kitchen base ~900 mm (36 in) high / counters ~625 mm (25 in) deep — Canadian typical, not a code. CLASS cabinets.
tools_equipment: Named: shims (wood shingles); finish nails; nail set. Not a SKU list.
inspection_hold_points: Wall/ceiling finishes complete before floor coverings (Ch22).
Wood strip after concrete has cured and gypsum is finished (Ch22).
Door frame plumb/square; shims at hinges and latch; nails in pairs (Ch23).
Casings 3/16–1/4 in off jamb, finish nails 16 in OC (Ch23).
typical_duration_sfr: CMHC Ch2: interior finishes about two weeks; paint/cabinets/fixtures about two weeks — Canadian sample. No lag days invented.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Flooring before drywall is done. Inventing a coat schedule. Selling a brand cabinet as the book SOP.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They know trim. What they skip is floors after walls/ceilings, and shims at hinge and latch.
permit_gate: not a new type — finishes follow drawings
risk_if_swapped_late: Hardwood before humidity is down is a gap/cup callback (Ch22).
plain_language_summary: Rock is up. Then doors and casing — shims at the hinges and the latch, finish nails 16 inches. Paint. Floors last, after the walls are done and the basement slab has dried. Do not invent a paint schedule.
spanish_summary: El drywall ya esta. Luego puertas y casing — cuñas en bisagras y cerradura, clavos de acabado a 16 pulgadas. Pintura. Pisos al final, paredes listas y la losa seca. No invente un horario de pintura.
